clue.text: Long narrative again provided by Indian chief

parts.note: a saga is a long story, originally a Norse epic
more means further, once again, as in 'do it some more'

explanation.surface: A long story is told once more by a Native American chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A sagamore was a subordinate chief among the Algonquian peoples of North America.

clue.text: Picking us up, heading off home perhaps

indicators.note: picking something up in a down clue lifts it, reading it from the bottom upwards
in a down entry 'up' means the letters are written bottom to top
heading off means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the newspaper speaking of itself: 'us' is The Times, the paper printing the clue

explanation.surface: Someone collects us and then sets off for home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' is The Times itself. 'Heading off' drops its T, leaving IMES, and 'Picking ... up' turns that over in this down clue, giving SEMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi, short for semi-detached house, is an example of a home; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Costliest purge, I suspect, is a way to please some of the voters

definitions.text: a way to please some of the voters

indicators.note: I suspect reads as an adjective for something dubious, so the preceding letters are treated as unreliable and rearranged

explanation.surface: A commentator suspects an expensive party purge is a ploy to win over part of the electorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' looks like an aside, but 'suspect' is the anagram signal working on COSTLIEST, PURGE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Gesture politics means symbolic actions meant to impress a section of the electorate rather than achieve real change.

clue.text: Boss in red-top office reflected

parts.note: red-top is British slang for a tabloid, from the red mastheads; the Daily Mirror is one
the editor, ED, is the boss in a newspaper office

explanation.surface: The chief in a tabloid newspaper's office is being echoed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mirror is a British tabloid of the kind called red-tops after their red title banners; its boss is its editor, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mirrored is reflected, as in a looking glass.

clue.text: In official costume, run carrying weight, not getting to the finish

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

indicators.note: a word not getting to its finish stops short and loses its final letter

parts.note: carrying excess weight means being obese

explanation.surface: Someone in ceremonial dress runs while overweight and fails to complete the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not getting to the finish' trims the last E from OBESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Robes are the formal gowns worn by judges, clergy and dignitaries on official occasions.

clue.text: It's right for individual to let go of son

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: letting go of means releasing, so these letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: an individual is a person
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is it fair for a person to give up on their child?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to let go of' removes SON from PERSON, leaving PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and right are synonyms, as in 'the proper way to do it'.

clue.text: Someone selling amateur recording

parts.note: a rep, short for sales representative, sells for a firm
lay means non-professional, as in 'lay person'

explanation.surface: A salesman makes a homemade tape.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay is a playing again of a recording, such as action shown again on television.

clue.text: On office desk you may find that perennials perch precariously

definitions.text: On office desk you may find that

indicators.note: something perched precariously is unstable and liable to topple, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Potted perennial plants balance unsteadily on someone's office desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precariously' is the anagram signal for PERENNIALS and PERCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil sharpener is a typical item of stationery kept on a desk at work.

clue.text: Orange and reds could make for pretty backyard

indicators.note: could make means these letters can be refashioned into something new

explanation.surface: Orange and red flowers would make a garden look attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' is the anagram signal for ORANGE and REDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose garden is a cultivated plot of roses, an attractive kind of garden.

clue.text: Faithful servant makes any number of pounds for trader

indicators.note: makes here says one letter becomes another, the first turned into the second

parts.note: a retainer is a long-serving household servant
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A loyal servant earns a fortune as a merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' turns the N (any number) in RETAINER into L (pounds).
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer is a trader who sells goods to the public.

clue.text: Note monarch in black, sorrowful

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: in means the monarch is placed inside the word for black

parts.note: sable is the heraldic word for black
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen dressed in black is in mourning.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable and sorrowful both mean deeply unhappy.

clue.text: Drinks assigned marks (zero not given)

indicators.note: not given means this letter is left out of the word

parts.note: marks in a test or game are points
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Someone is awarded a score of nothing for their drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not given' removes the O (zero) from POINTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pints are glasses of beer, the standard drinks measure in a British pub.

clue.text: Goddess in boat with love for king

indicators.note: love for king means the letter for love takes the place of the letter for king

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing boat
K is the abbreviation for king in chess
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A goddess sits in a boat with her beloved instead of the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts O (love) in place of K (king) in JUNK.
explanation.definitionFit: Juno was the Roman queen of the gods, wife of Jupiter.

clue.text: Those afar in Grenada some as sailors

indicators.note: some means only a part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: People far away in Grenada are a seagoing lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to letters running through 'thoSE AFAR IN Grenada'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seafaring describes people who travel by sea, as sailors do.

clue.text: God bearing fruit in magnificent manifestation

indicators.note: in places everything before it inside the word for magnificent

parts.note: ace means excellent, first-rate

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the god holds the fruit within

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A deity laden with fruit makes a splendid show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' and 'in' are both container signals, nested: the fruit sits inside the god, and that pair sits inside the word for magnificent.
explanation.definitionFit: An appearance is a manifestation, the act of showing up or becoming visible.

clue.text: About to have egg producers in large building, making a clutch possible

indicators.note: in means the preceding letters go inside the word for a building

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building such as a mansion
re means about, concerning
hens lay eggs

explanation.surface: Soon to keep laying hens in a big house, with a nest of eggs possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutch' looks like a set of eggs, matching the hens, but here it means gripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehensile describes a tail or limb able to grasp, as a monkey's tail can.

clue.text: Label in bank maybe to show deficit

indicators.note: in means the label is placed inside the word for bank

parts.note: a shore is a kind of bank, of sea or lake; 'maybe' marks the example
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A tag on a bank account reveals it is overdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money, but it is the shore of a body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage is a deficit, an amount by which something falls short.

clue.text: Druggie one who thinks head will float off

indicators.note: the head floating off means the first letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a muser is someone who ponders or thinks

explanation.surface: A drug taker believes their head will drift away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head will float off' drops the M from MUSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for a drug addict.

clue.text: It's horrible, leader not being seen or properly recognised

indicators.note: the leader not being seen means the first letter of the word disappears

parts.note: frightful means horrible, dreadful

explanation.surface: It's awful that the leader is absent, someone complains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader not being seen' drops the F from FRIGHTFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Rightful means legitimately or properly acknowledged, as in the rightful owner.

clue.text: Biblical land way back

indicators.note: back means the word for way is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner

explanation.surface: A Biblical country found by going backwards along a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MODE round.
explanation.definitionFit: Edom was an ancient kingdom south of the Dead Sea, named in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Harmonise with new decoration

indicators.note: new means the letters of the word are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Bring things together with fresh decor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal for DECORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: To coordinate is to bring elements into harmony so they work together.

clue.text: Tom's a bit confused inside — one going this way and that?

definitions.text: one going this way and that

indicators.note: a bit confused inside means only a little shuffling in the middle of the surname

parts.note: Tom Sawyer is Mark Twain's boy hero, so Tom's surname is Sawyer

explanation.surface: Tom is slightly muddled inside, as if he keeps swaying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit confused inside' swaps the inner A and W of SAWYER, Tom Sawyer being the boy hero of Mark Twain's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A swayer is someone or something that sways, moving from side to side.

clue.text: Terrain was almost cracking — need for this?

definitions.text: Terrain was almost cracking — need for this?

indicators.note: cracking means breaking apart, so these letters split and re-form
almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

explanation.surface: Parched ground split open, crying out for a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims WAS to WA; 'cracking' rearranges TERRAIN and WA. Read whole, the clue describes ground so dry it cracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracked, drought-hit ground needs rain falling on it, water from the sky.

clue.text: Stick used by one laying down the line

definitions.meaning: a straight measuring stick for drawing lines
a monarch or leader who lays down the law, the official line

explanation.surface: A ruled stick wielded by someone who sets strict rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a straight-edged measuring rod, and a sovereign who decides policy.

clue.text: The fellow without work, and the virtue he needs?

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the fellow wraps around the word for work

parts.note: he refers to a man, the fellow
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: An unemployed man needs optimism above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is its old sense 'outside'. Hope is one of the three theological virtues with faith and charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope is one of the three theological virtues, alongside faith and charity, and a jobless man needs it.

clue.text: Bird to sink down gripping end of branch

indicators.note: gripping means holding, so the sink word wraps around the letter

parts.note: to sag is to sink or droop

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A bird drops down while clutching the tip of a branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives H from branch; 'gripping' puts it inside SAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A shag is a seabird of the cormorant family.

clue.text: One stabbing of facial feature? Not really ear-piercing maybe!

indicators.note: stabbing means piercing, so the numeral is thrust into the word

parts.note: nosy read literally as relating to the nose, a facial feature
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A nose-piercing, it turns out, is not an ear-piercing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ear-piercing' looks like jewellery talk but means loud. 'Not really' admits that NOSY means prying rather than belonging to a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear-piercing noise is very loud, so ear-piercing describes something noisy.

clue.text: Bird in Bond film bumping off German companion

indicators.note: bumping off means killing, so the German is removed and replaced by the companion

parts.note: Goldfinger is the 1964 James Bond film
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A bird appears in a 007 film in which a German companion is murdered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumping off' removes GER (German) from GOLDFINGER and puts CH (Companion of Honour) in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldfinch is a small brightly coloured finch with a gold wing bar.

clue.text: Guarantee result will be about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for result goes around the letter

parts.note: to ensue is to follow as a result

explanation.surface: A promise that the outcome will be correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ENSUE around R.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain, to guarantee that something happens.

clue.text: Excavate either side of stream and river — means to get at oil maybe

definitions.text: means to get at oil maybe

indicators.note: being on either side of means the dig word wraps around what follows

parts.note: to dig is to excavate
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Someone digs on both banks of a brook and river to reach oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either side of' makes the excavating word wrap the stream and river. 'Excavate' tempts the solver to take DRILL from it directly.
explanation.definitionFit: A drilling rig is the structure used to bore wells, for example to extract petroleum.
